info.title: Unmade Integration Reference V2
info.description:
Welcome to the Unmade OS Integration Reference.

See [Integrating With Unmade](#/group-integrating-with-unmade) to get started.

This is **Version 2** of this documentation, which describes the usage of the `v2` API Endpoints. For **Version 1**, [click here](https://engineering.unmade.com/api-docs/#/).

get.description:
The response to this request is a well-formed HTML document used as content for the `<iframe>`.

Use this URL as the `src` attribute value on an `<iframe>` element to embed an Unmade-powered product in an
external e-commerce website.  Note that there are optional query parameters.

Depending on your specific editor UI design and the rest of the content on the page you are embedding the Unmade Iframe on, you might need to take different approaches to managing the size of the `<iframe>` element on the page. We are happy to advise and support on this.

post.description:
Once an order has been placed on the ecommerce platform, the Unmade system should be notified to begin the process of
generating manufacturing files. To do this, pass a unique order reference, and one or more order items to this endpoint
via an HTTP POST request. Each item must reference an Unmade Design ID. The same Design ID can be used for multiple
order items, if provided with different `size` values inside the `options` object. To order multiple identical garments
in the same size, use the `quantity` value. Each item must also have a `unit_price` object with both a `value` and
`currency` specified. Depending on the nature of your integration with Unmade, a `shipping_address` may also be required
for order creation.

Optionally, arbitrary key-value pairs can be passed as a `partner_data` object at both the order and order item level. 
This may be used by your system to provide your internal ID or similar reference for this order which may be relevant
for integration with your vendor. These key-value pairs will also be present on the manufacturing order and jobs 
associated with this ecommerce order.

If you want to create the order and keep it on hold for subsequent updates to the `partner_data` you might do it by
sending the boolean value for `set_order_on_hold` as `true`.

You may optionally provide a boolean value for the `is_test_order` field to indicate a given order is not a real
production order. If this value is set to `true`, the order will be omitted from Unmade billing processes. Speak to your
Unmade representative for more information about recommended integration testing procedures.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: e.g. Token ABCDEF

reference.description: Your unique reference for this order. Max 256 characters.

order_items.description: One or more items to include in the order.

partner_data.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs to associate with the order as a whole (e.g. PO number, shipping method).

address_1.description: First line of address. Max 256 characters.

address_2.description: Second line of address. Max 256 characters.

postal_code.description: Postal or ZIP code. Max 20 characters.

country_area.description: State, province, or region. Max 128 characters.

get.description:
This endpoint can be used to retrieve a paginated list of the individual items in a given order. We preserve the order
in which the items were sent in the original order creation payload. The `id` of each item is generated automatically
by Unmade when the order is created. You may choose to store this ID in your systems in order to reference each item
directly in future.

Each order item has three associated Design IDs which have different relationships depending on how the relevant 
designs were created, as well as the type of order. In the simplest case these Design IDs may be identical, but will 
usually be different, depending on a variety of factors.

- `input_design_id`: The Design ID which you originally sent in the Order creation payload to create this item

- `manufacturing_design_id`: The ID of the design which is being used as the source of all manufacturing data for this 
    item. This will be different to the `input_design_id` if you specified a different size to that of the order 
    item design: in this case Unmade will generate a new design in the specified size

- `source_design_id`: The ID of the Design which was originally saved by the user in the editor. If the Roster API has 
    been used to create the member design for this item, this ID will be the ID of the original roster **template** 
    design.

These Design IDs can be used in the Design API to view personalisation data or fetch previews relevant to this order 
item. In most cases you'll want to use the `design_id` value for this purpose.

post.description:
On creation, Unmade assigns all production jobs an Ex-factory date based on a lead time estimate which has been 
pre-agreed with you and your vendor. This serves as a target date by which the piece is expected to have left the 
factory location. Jobs within an order can have different Ex-factory dates depending on per-product lead times. In the 
case of unforeseen delays (or unexpectedly quicker production!) this endpoint can be used to pass an updated Ex-factory 
date to Unmade. If provided, all jobs in the given order are assigned this updated Ex-factory date. This update also 
propagates up to this order's associated Ecommerce order to allow the Ecommerce system to notify to the end-consumer.

get.description:
This endpoint can be used to retrieve data for a specific job in a given order. In addition to basic metadata, this 
endpoint provides:

- Structured data describing the various customisation options chosen by the user for this job (eg. selected 
   **components**, **text** and **colours**)

- URLs to one or more `previews` for this job

- The URL for a zip file containing all manufacturing files for this job

- The URL to this job's ticket PDF

### Job States

Jobs flow through the same states as [orders](#/group-factory-api#header-order-states), but jobs within an order may each have different states.

Jobs also have an additional state: `not_ready` which is used when a given job has been very recently created. This state indicates that manufacturing files are still being generated and are not yet available for download.  You will notice that the `manufacturing_files_zip` field will be `null` for jobs which are still in the `not_ready` state.

When a job progresses from state `not_ready` to `new`, the `manufacturing_files_zip` URL will become available. This means that all manufacturing files are ready, and the URL can then be used to download all manufacturing files for a given job.

The URLs provided by the `manufacturing_files_zip` and `ticket` fields do not require authentication, so can be safely stored and passed to any other systems that may be part of your order management workflow.

state of this job's order to `in_production`, but does not affect the state of the other jobs in this order.
